name: grep
summary: Search text for lines that match
tasks: search all files in a folder

examples.does: Lines containing 'error', any case
Search every file in a folder, with file names and line numbers
The settings only, without comments and blank lines
Count lines matching either word
Each match with 2 lines before and 3 after
Only the names of .conf files that contain a word

pitfalls: Quote the pattern. Without quotes the shell may change it (e.g. * or |).
grep -E is for extended patterns such as a|b; plain grep treats | as a normal character.

name: sed
summary: Edit text: print parts, replace, delete lines
tasks: print some lines of a file
edit a config file in place

examples.does: Print lines 10 to 20 only
Print the file with every 'old' replaced; the file is not changed
Edit the file in place, keeping the original as .bak
Delete empty lines from the file

pitfalls: Run without -i first and read the output. -i writes straight to the file.
Give -i a suffix (-i.bak) to keep the original.

name: awk
summary: Pick out columns and compute over lines of text
tasks: top client IPs in a web log

examples.does: The 10 client IPs with the most requests
Normal user accounts (UID 1000 and up)
Filesystems more than 80% full
Pass a value in from the shell (-v)
Add up a column (here: bytes sent)

pitfalls: Ubuntu's default awk is mawk. GNU awk extensions such as gensub() need the gawk package.
Use single quotes around the program, or the shell replaces $1 before awk sees it.

name: sort

examples.does: Sort lines alphabetically
Sort human-readable sizes (K, M, G) correctly
Sort and drop duplicate lines
Sort by the 3rd ':'-separated column, as numbers

pitfalls: Plain sort puts 10 before 9. Use -n for numbers and -h for sizes.

name: uniq
summary: Collapse or count repeated lines (input must be sorted)

examples.does: How often each line occurs, most frequent first
Only lines that occur more than once

pitfalls: uniq only merges lines that are next to each other. Sort first.

name: cut
summary: Pick out columns by a separator

examples.does: The first ':'-separated column (account names)
Columns 2 and 4 of a simple CSV

pitfalls: cut splits on one character exactly. For columns separated by several spaces, use awk.

examples.does: Each PATH entry on its own line
Remove Windows carriage returns (writes a new file)

name: xargs
summary: Run a command with input lines as its arguments
tasks: run a command for each line

examples.does: Delete what find found, safe with spaces in names
Run one command per input line
Run up to 4 at a time

pitfalls: Without -print0 and -0, file names with spaces split into several arguments.

name: tee
summary: Write to a file and the screen at once
tasks: append to a file with sudo

examples.does: Write a root-owned file (sudo echo > file does not work: the shell opens the file, not sudo)
Append a line instead of replacing the file

pitfalls: Without -a, tee replaces the whole file.

name: column
tasks: make output readable as a table

examples.does: Line up whitespace-separated output
Show a simple CSV as a table
